newsitem.title: USA: Sears hit with class-action suit - lawyers.
newsitem.headline: Sears hit with class-action suit - lawyers.

text.p: A class action lawsuit was filed against Sears, Roebuck and Co in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois on April 15, the plaintiffs' lawyers said on Tuesday.

The complaint alleges that certain officers and directors of Sears failed to disclose that the firm coerced certain individual debtors in bankruptcy and Sears card holders into signing reaffirmation agreements concerning those debts.
Sears then failed to file those agreements with the Bankruptcy Court as required by law, the lawyers alleged.

They allege that because of the issuance of false and misleading statements concerning Sears' business practices, Sears common stock was artificially inflated between October 4, 1996 and April 10, 1997.

On April 10, 1997, Sears announced that it would be voluntarily repaying Chapter 7 bankruptcy debtors nationwide whose debt reaffirmations were not filed with the U.S. Bankruptcy Court as required by law.
The suit was filed on behalf of holders who purchased or acquired Sears stock between October 4, 1996 and April 10, 1997.

The plaintiffs seek to recover damages on behalf of class members and are represented by the law firms of Milberg Weiss Bershad Hynes & Lerach LLP, Schiffrin & Craig, Ltd, Miller Faucher Chertow Cafferty and Wexler and the Offices of Alfred Yates Jr.
